policy.mapping_basis: test method names and bodies in staging/xr-ui-shell, matched against contract clause text; the code has not compiled or executed

clauses.clause: shell surface identity: PanelId, WristMenuId, and HandMenuId with a canonical form, rejection of empty, whitespace, and malformed identifiers with a stable identity.malformed failure, value equality between two identities of the same type with the same text, and no equality across types; InputSourceId shares the same rules

a shell layout model: a panel declaration names one closed anchor kind and the closed set of anchor kinds it admits; a wrist menu admits only wrist and a hand menu admits only hand; declaring a panel id twice is rejected with panel.duplicate; a declared layout enumerates its surfaces and registered input sources in canonical order

intent application to an immutable shell state with stable failure codes: an intent naming an undeclared panel is rejected with panel.unknown; a dock or follow intent whose target anchor kind the panel does not admit is rejected with anchor.kind.unsupported; a focus intent while another open panel holds exclusive focus is rejected with focus.conflict; at most one panel is focused at any time; an accepted dock or follow intent updates the docked target, the follow flag, and the current anchor kind; closing the focused panel clears focus

state immutability: a state is immutable, an accepted intent produces a new state and leaves the prior state intact, and a rejected intent leaves the prior state intact and returns it unchanged with the failure code

deterministic replay: the same intent sequence over the same declarations and initial state produces an equal final state and an equal fingerprint, and a state enumerates every declared panel with its current anchor kind, open flag, docked target, follow flag, the focused panel, and the registered input sources

pointer and gaze routing as typed intents: hover, select, and scroll each carry a registered InputSourceId plus the candidate panel set the adapter observed; routing resolves to exactly one open panel, prefers the exclusively focused panel when it is a candidate, and otherwise returns route.ambiguous for two or more candidates and route.none for zero; a source that is not registered is rejected with source.unknown; a select or scroll from a gaze source without a registered commit source is rejected with source.kind.unsupported; a rejected routing intent changes no state

a skin contract: the design-language tokens map to a closed set of named shell slots; a mapping that names a token outside the design-language set is rejected with token.unknown, a mapping that names a slot outside the closed set is rejected with slot.unknown, and a skin that leaves any slot without a mapping is rejected with slot.unmapped; the canonical mapping resolves every slot

structured results with stable failure codes for a malformed identity, an unknown or duplicate panel, an unsupported anchor kind, a focus conflict, an unknown source, an unsupported source kind, an ambiguous or empty route, an unknown token, an unknown slot, and an unmapped slot, each carrying the offending field path, plus a valid intent sequence passing clean with every outcome accepted
the Core references no engine type, reads no input device, computes no pose, raycast, or world-space transform, holds no colour or size value, and renders nothing

the ornament: one shell-owned fixed surface, never folded. It is not declared by a consumer and never enters a built ShellLayout's declared-surface set or SurfaceCount, but its identity is fixed and reachable from any state; a fold or unfold intent naming it is always rejected with a stable code

a verb registry: a closed, explicitly registered id set; an unregistered verb is rejected with a stable code and never silently absorbed into another verb or dropped; registered ids partition into wired and unwired; and a verb has one constant id and display word, fixed at registration, regardless of the target it later resolves against

a single-valued FocusSubject claimed only by an explicit focus intent: a per-frame mirror or sync of Current never claims; an assignment (Claim) always replaces the whole value rather than merging with the prior one; and there is exactly one current target (a panel, a panel item, or an external target path) or none

verb resolution reads only the current FocusSubject value, with no precedence chain and no branch order over any other source, and yields exactly one resolved target or a named no-target result; an unregistered or unwired verb is rejected with its own stable code; and two different verbs resolved against the same FocusSubject value always agree on the target

a queryable pre-press affordance per registered verb: the resolved target name, available or unavailable, and a stable reason code, so a verb is never shown available for a target it would in fact refuse (the affordance's availability and reason always agree with what VerbResolver.Resolve would do for the same registry, verb, and subject)

fold retains state: a folded surface keeps its full open, docked-target, and follow state; fold and unfold are intents that change only visibility (SurfaceRuntimeState.IsFolded); and fold/unfold of an undeclared surface is rejected with panel.unknown exactly like open/close/focus/dock/follow

one intent channel for people and agents (LESSON-011): every placement ShellIntent (open, close, focus, dock, follow, fold, unfold) carries an IntentActor from the closed set player/agent/replay/import, defaulting to player when a caller does not name one, and an optional expected revision; ShellState carries a monotonically increasing Revision, 0 for Initial and one higher on every accepted intent, excluded from Fingerprint

a stale expected revision is rejected with state.stale and changes nothing: ShellState.Apply checks a non-null expected revision before the intent's own rule ever runs, for every placement intent type and regardless of actor

the actor never changes validation: a player-issued and an agent-issued copy of the same placement intent, accepted or rejected, take the same path through ShellState.Apply and produce an equal result (same accepted flag and code) and, when accepted, an equal resulting state and revision

the same shape on a verb press and the replay log: a dock verb pressed by a person and the same verb issued by an agent adapter resolve through the same FocusSubject value and the same VerbAffordanceQuery/VerbResolver reads (neither takes an actor), and applying the resulting DockIntent from each actor onto an equal initial state produces equal outcomes and an equal resulting state; ShellIntentOutcome (from ApplyAll) carries the issuing intent's actor and the state's revision immediately after the outcome settled, accepted or rejected

a thin binding of each declared panel to exactly one world-space Canvas subtree, with stable codes, field paths, and the source asset for a missing Canvas reference (surface.missing), a Canvas whose render mode is not world space (surface.mode.mismatch), a Canvas bound to two panels (surface.duplicate), a missing event camera (camera.missing), a missing tracked-device graphic raycaster (raycaster.missing), a scene without exactly one active XR UI input module (input.module.missing), and a wrist or hand anchor whose transform reference is missing (anchor.target.missing), and construction that throws with the same report

an explicit diagnostic for every by-name or optional resolution: an interactor member, an input action reference, an anchor transform, a Canvas component, or a sprite that the adapter resolves by name, by serialized field, or by an optional lookup must report an explicit failure with a stable code when the target is missing or incompatible, and must carry a negative test for the missing target (LESSON-004); silence or a reported success is a defect

one injectable skin seam, a ScriptableObject mapping the shared design-language tokens to the closed slot set, applied through one entry point on the panel runtime and propagated to every bound Canvas subtree, with a default skin asset carrying the canonical token values so an un-themed install already matches the shared look (LESSON-007); no colour, radius, or hit-size value lives in a serialized per-view field or an editor factory constant

translation of accepted routing results: the adapter reports the candidate panel set from the raycaster to the Core, forwards a resolved hover, select, or scroll to the bound Canvas only, and forwards nothing on route.ambiguous, route.none, or any rejection

a runtime constructed with explicit references that applies accepted placement intents to the bound anchors in the order they were accepted and reports accepted and rejected state, with no scene singleton, static instance, scene search, or reflection discovery
two independent runtimes constructed side by side over two Canvas sets that share no state and do not interfere with each other's anchors, skins, or routing

one intent channel, no second write path (LESSON-011): the runtime writes state only by constructing a ShellIntent and passing it to ShellState.Apply, never by calling a Core mutator directly, tested by a source rule over every Runtime .cs file; and a player-issued and an agent-issued copy of the same intent take the same path and produce an equal resulting state

a thin binding of each declared panel to exactly one world-space UIDocument, with stable codes, field paths, and the source asset for a missing document reference (surface.missing), PanelSettings whose render mode is not world space (surface.mode.mismatch), a document bound to two panels (surface.duplicate), a document without a collider or with a collider update mode the composition does not admit (collider.missing), a scene without exactly one active XR UI Toolkit manager (input.module.missing), a manager or panel that bypasses UI Toolkit events (input.bypassed), and a wrist or hand anchor whose transform reference is missing (anchor.target.missing), and construction that throws with the same report

an explicit diagnostic for every by-name or optional resolution: a VisualElement looked up by name, a USS class or variable applied by name, a PanelSettings property read by reflection, or an interactor member resolved by an optional lookup must report an explicit failure with a stable code when the target is missing or incompatible, and must carry a negative test for the missing target (LESSON-004); silence or a reported success is a defect

one injectable skin seam, a skin object that maps the shared design-language tokens to the closed slot set and applies them as USS variables or classes on the bound document root, with a default skin carrying the canonical token values (LESSON-007); the seam is the only place that writes visual values into the document

translation of accepted routing results to the bound document only, forwarding nothing on route.ambiguous, route.none, or any rejection, under the same clauses as the UGUI adapter gate, against UIDocument roots instead of Canvas subtrees

a runtime constructed with explicit references that applies accepted placement intents to the bound document subtrees in the order they were accepted and reports accepted and rejected state, with no scene singleton, static instance, scene search, or reflection discovery
two independent runtimes constructed side by side over two document sets that share no state and do not interfere with each other's anchors, skins, or routing

one intent channel, no second write path (LESSON-011): the runtime writes state only by constructing a ShellIntent and passing it to ShellState.Apply, never by calling a Core mutator directly, tested by a source rule over every Runtime .cs file; and a player-issued and an agent-issued copy of the same intent take the same path and produce an equal resulting state

summary.execution_note: All 112 tests (71 Core including 2 source-rule tests outside the numbered clauses, 20 UGUI adapter, 21 UI Toolkit adapter) are authored in staging and have never compiled or run; the first Unity run either confirms them or turns this map red. WI-023 added six Core clauses (XUC-10..XUC-15: the ornament, the verb registry, FocusSubject, verb resolution, the pre-press affordance, and fold state retention) and inverted the shell/Live Tuning dependency: the UGUI adapter no longer references Lingkyn.LiveTuning.*, its former Live Tuning integration test moved to staging/live-tuning/com.lingkyn.live-tuning.unity, and a new source-rule test proves no asmdef under staging/xr-ui-shell references any assembly outside Lingkyn.XrUiShell.* (plus the admitted engine/test assemblies) and no shell Runtime .cs mentions LiveTuning, Inventory, Settings, or another family namespace. WI-024 added the one-intent-channel actor/expected-revision/state.stale shape (LESSON-011): Core clauses XUC-16..19 give every placement ShellIntent an IntentActor and an optional expected revision, ShellState carries a monotonically increasing Revision excluded from the fingerprint, a stale expected revision is rejected with state.stale regardless of actor, and a dock verb pressed by a person and issued by an agent resolve through the same FocusSubject and affordance and settle on an equal state; CUG-07 and CUT-07 add the matching source rule and player/agent equivalence test to each renderer adapter, which already wrote state only through ShellState.Apply. Every clause is proven against a fake or a plain constructed Unity component for every seam (ISkinTarget-style targets, IUguiRoutedEventTarget, IUiToolkitRoutedEventTarget, IUiToolkitInputManager) and no test claims that a panel was visible, legible, or reachable, that an anchor followed a wrist or hand, that a ray or gaze hit a panel on a device, or that any input was read from a device; those claims stay with a Device Lab receipt per the claim ceiling.
